thesis: Juzám Djinn made black’s life-for-power bargain visible on the battlefield: four mana bought a 5/5 whose upkeep damage mattered only if the opponent survived long enough to exploit it.

playbook.role: Treat the Djinn as a clock, not a value engine. Build the mana to cast it reliably, clear blockers before committing it, and measure every point of self-damage against the number of attacks needed to end the game.

counterplay.directAnswers: Use unconditional removal, larger blockers, or a race that turns the upkeep trigger into a real liability. Chump blocking is worthwhile only when the extra turn changes the opposing clock or exposes the Djinn’s controller to burn.
